description: Experimental prerelease candidate that carries the seven stack B decisions of bsv-blockchain/dpp#177: @bsv/dpp-protocol and @bsv/dpp-profiles move to 0.3.0-beta.10 and @bsv/dpp-overlay to 0.4.0-beta.13, and @bsv/dpp-credentials to 0.2.0-beta.6, which keeps external credential verification and the EPCIS source helpers and no longer contains the parked VSC compatibility profile, its Ed25519Signature2020 and bbs-2023 proof suites or the EPCIS-to-SEAL mappings. The verification report checks token payloads against their declared profile through a caller-supplied validator; restricted tiers are disclosed per reader; acceptance records travel in the evidence package; the native claim names its state by outpoint; the index contract is 0.14.0-draft, with per-publisher write tokens bound to one key and one use and self-service registration through POST /register, a wallet-signed dpp-index-registration@1 request that appends an operator-signed policy version and returns those tokens, and the registry contract 0.6.0, which adds the envelope of the proposed epcis-event-vc@1, refuses a submission of the parked vsc-seal-json-v1 as unsupported and defines no status list publication. From 12 November 2026 the native claim carries no evidence facets; the index contract separates a core, version 1, from versioned extensions, and its refusal codes are informative; the registry contract is the minimum every registry serves and has no legacy intake, so a historical UORA body is refused while stored historical records stay readable; the one export format is dpp-evidence-package@1 per passport, signed by the BRC-42 child of the exporter's identity key named in its capability document, and the multi-part export and the index's history pages are reference features of @bsv/dpp-overlay; and the application interoperability API contract is the reference application's own. The custody profile is managed-custody@2, the one custody profile: the custodian signs its acceptance records with a derived key through the wallet's createSignature, and dpp-managed-acceptance@1 records are read and never written. From 12 November 2026 the owner-signed transfer for version 1 lineages is removed from the standard, and the holder instruction record and record version 3, the token carrier, are parked outside it, so the set names record versions 1 and 2 and verification report version 2. From the same day the selection requires one claim per role under native-baseline@2, the one baseline a claim names, with gs1-identifier-discipline and profile-governance, and withholds every other claim, among them those of the optional custody, exchange and EPCIS profiles. From the same day passport projections and the publication policy are reference features of @bsv/dpp-profiles, whose source and projection schemas moved from contracts/ into that package; the GS1 discovery specification keeps only the DPP identifier rules; the publisher policy chain, write tokens, registration operations and synchronisation are reference features of @bsv/dpp-overlay, with SHIP/SLAP discovery and federated-operators@1 parked; the drafts battery@3, textile@3 and textile@4 are parked with their bytes unchanged; and spec/rules.md section 4 is the one definition of the canonical JSON the native documents use. Package publication does not establish deployment readiness or product qualification.

dependencies.name: mongodb
dependencies.note: the reference persistence of the index node, replaceable

dependencies.name: @bsv/wallet-toolbox-client
dependencies.note: the application service's wallet, and from this set an optional dependency of @bsv/dpp-overlay for advertising, at the same version; npm install --omit=optional leaves it out

packages.name: @bsv/dpp-protocol
packages.role: the passport record models, signatures, custody rules, chain and evidence verification, native lifecycle claims, attestation anchors, publisher policies and portable evidence

support.notes: Depends on @bsv/sdk only and imports no Node built-in; a browser bundle is not tested and not promised.
Normative JSON schemas copied byte for byte from contracts; relative schema references remain alongside one another.

packages.name: @bsv/dpp-overlay
packages.role: the topic managers, lookup services, storage adapters, capabilities, history, evidence export, retraction and synchronisation of the index; a supported server entry point and dpp-index executable also run the HTTP node

support.notes: Server only: Node built-ins, the overlay engine and the MongoDB driver. Importing never starts the HTTP host.
HTTP host and runFromEnvironment for an operator process. Importing starts nothing; the dpp-index executable calls the runner explicitly.

packages.name: @bsv/dpp-profiles
packages.role: the industry, exchange and operator profiles as frozen manifests with generated schemas and consumer documents, the lifecycle mapping for both record versions, and the GS1 identifier helpers; the GS1 discovery helpers, the interoperability manifests, the shared evidence shapes, the declarative applicability evaluator and the deterministic passport projection; structural profile change reports and version 4 cross-field data review

support.notes: Reads its data files through the Node file system; the one runtime dependency is the RFC 8785 canonicaliser.
The manifest, identity, exchange, operator and interoperability schemas and the pinned GS1 resolver schemas.
Generated payload schemas, consumer documents and mapping inventories.
The digests every published file is held to.

packages.name: @bsv/dpp-credentials
packages.role: external W3C Verifiable Credential 2.0 verification under ecdsa-rdfc-2019 over P-256 from did:web issuers, with authenticated Bitstring Status List status and bounded did:web resolution (./exchange), and the EPCIS source helpers with the pinned EPCIS 2.0.1 artefacts (./epcis-source); the root re-exports the EPCIS source helpers, strict parsing and did:web resolution and loads no proof suite. The parked VSC draft compatibility profile, its two proof suites and the EPCIS-to-SEAL mappings are no longer in the package, which keeps the owned context and schema artefacts their parked manifests pin

support.notes: Server only: reads its pinned EPCIS artefacts through the file system.
The external ecdsa-rdfc-2019 credential verifier; server only: reads its artefacts through the file system and decompresses status lists with node:zlib.
The EPCIS source helpers; server only for the same reasons.

The pinned EPCIS and W3C artefacts and the external passport context and schema, each with a notice file naming its digest, and the owned context and schemas of the parked VSC profile, kept because its manifests pin them, with their digests in profile-0.1.0.json.

alsoSupported: managed-custody@1 records, read under spec/managed-custody.md section 9 and never written

serviceInterface.note: PassportService in the reference application, whose source is not public, is the account-agnostic entry point over the writer's journal; it consumes the packages above and is not itself published in this set.

artefacts.pins: the baseline this set claims, with every fixture digest
the index's HTTP contract: the core, version 1, and its versioned extensions
the report schema and reason codes
the version 1 report schema, under which a stored version 1 report validates
the capability document, naming the identity key whose derived child signs each evidence package
the shared evidence, measurement, certification, document and language shapes of spec/profiles.md section 3
the acceptance record a managed custodian signs with its derived key, with its binding and seven refusals
the registration request an application's wallet signs with its derived key, the index's expectations and seven refusals
the native claim with its outpoint recordId and the anchor over its bytes
the same claim and anchor in the stack vector format, with the six refusals only this form carries

the registry contract, the minimum every registry serves, with the claim schema that refuses any recordId but an outpoint, the envelope of the proposed epcis-event-vc@1, the refusal of the parked vsc-seal-json-v1, no legacy intake and no status list routes

consumers.name: the reference application
consumers.consumes: exact npm dependencies; adoption of @bsv/dpp-profiles 0.3.0-beta.9 and explicit profile activation require a separate application change
consumers.note: the example consumer with sector workflows; package installation, supported readers and selected writers are separate adoption decisions

consumers.name: the reference registry
consumers.consumes: the packages as vendored tarballs, to be replaced by the published packages of this set

consumers.name: a second stack under the same administration
consumers.consumes: the packages through public entry points at exact public registry versions
consumers.note: an index, registry, writer and reader application built from the public documentation, repository and packages alone; a reference consumer under the same administration, not an independent implementation, and no federated operation claim
